Take it one step at a time. If I were in your situation, here's what I'd do:

  1. Get your GED ASAP. A GED is the price of admission to your future career. Some people can get by without a high school education or GED, but they're anomalies. Us mere mortals need this basic credential.

  2. Get a "now" job. This doesn't have to be something you stick with forever; it's a job that pays the bills. Look at retail/bank teller/call center work...anything that will give you a consistent paycheck.

  3. Think about what kind of career interests you. Figure out what skillset is required. Figure out what gaps you need to overcome to acquire that skillset.

  4. Work to eliminate those gaps. Maybe you need to go to a trade school or get an apprenticeship. Maybe you need a college education. It really depends on what career you decide on.

Life can be difficult, and it isn't always fair. However, focusing on the past is not going to help you. If you want your life to change, you need to set goals and work to achieve them. 23 is still very young - you have a lot of life ahead of you. You have plenty of time to correct your course.

First off, you can relax. I was 23 when I decided to go back to school, and now I'm a college grad approaching 30 who still doesn't have life figured out. I don't think anyone ever does, so don't stress out over being 22 (which is super young) and not being totally sorted already.

Now, if you earn enough with your current job to support yourself getting a GED, then start the process ASAP. Remember to utilise all the support systems available (study groups, libraries, professors with open door policies) to help you achieve a passing grade. Don't be afraid to ask for help.

After you get the GED, start thinking about what jobs you would like to have. You seem to think academia isn't for you, so maybe you'd like to learn a trade or skill? There are plenty of options to consider, from cookery to mechanics to beauty school. Pick something you feel you can do that you would be happy with.

Once you've picked out a skill/trade, you need to look at how you can get in to it. Schools, apprenticeships, and 'working your way up' can all be really effective, depending on what you want to do. Go and talk to people. If you want to be a chef, speak to a chef in a restaurant and ask can you work as a kitchen porter while you learn the ropes. If you want to be a mechanic, find a garage that will let you do an apprenticeship. If you want to work in a salon, call the nearest beauty school and discuss your plans/options with them.

Another thing I will say (and it might not be popular), but don't stress so much about being a mooch either. I worked the whole time I was in college and got a partial scholarship, and I still don't think I could have afforded the graduate without my boyfriend covering some of my rent occasionally. We lived in an expensive city in Europe and I wasn't earning a lot. Any time I had to take time off to study or I got sick, I would be screwed, so he would cover me. As long as you are bettering yourself and not just being lazy, I think it's okay to ask your Mom if you can skip out on the rent once in a while (if she can afford it that is). It's better than throwing away your opportunities for a few extra bucks.

Get your education, find your passion, and pursue it with the intensity of 1,000 suns. Dont sacrifice anything but your whole life on your passion, and you will notice a drastic increase in your quality of life.
